additional.status_end_user_codes_diverge_from_resol: AC2 pins host.vault.status's own two failure codes to invalid_params (end_user omitted) and upstream_not_connected ("self" with no verified identity on the call), neither of which is what crate::enduser::resolve_end_user itself returns for the same inputs (args_invalid via AppError::InvalidArgs, and end_user_required respectively) -- the helper every other host.vault.* tool (connect_link, disconnect) already reuses unchanged. status therefore has its own small resolve_status_end_user: it short-circuits omitted/null and self-without-identity to the AC-pinned codes directly, and falls through to the shared resolve_end_user for every other shape (self-with-identity, a literal subject with no identity on the call, a literal subject WITH an identity -> end_user_explicit_forbidden), so AC2's first scenario (the tenant's own agent reading a literal subject) still resolves identically to connect_link's own behavior.
additional.status_provider_set_is_a_union_not_just_: AC6 requires that after host.vault.provider_remove deletes a provider's own vault_providers row, each previously-connected user's host.vault.status STILL names that provider (connected: false, revoked_reason: "provider_removed") -- so status cannot be driven by Db::list_vault_provider_names (the currently-registered set) alone. status instead unions that list with Db::list_vault_token_provider_names(tenant_id, subject) (new), which reads distinct provider names off vault_tokens itself for that one subject, registered or not. This keeps AC1's own case (every registered provider, connected or not) working identically, since a registered-but-never-connected provider (AC1's github) has no vault_tokens row and so is only found through the registered-providers half of the union.
additional.admin_vault_stats_tenant_id_field_is_the: admin.vault.stats's own requirement 2 names the field tenant_id, but this crate's own admin.mesh.stats precedent (MeshTenantStats.tenant) already established that a caller-facing per-tenant admin listing reports the tenant's namespace string, not its raw integer row id (which a caller has no way to have learned) -- Db::vault_stats's VaultTenantStats.tenant_id therefore holds the namespace, joined via `t.namespace` off `vault_tokens.tenant_id = t.id`, keeping the PRD's own field NAME while giving it the only value a real admin caller could actually match against (e.g. a namespace a prior admin.tenants/signup call already returned).
additional.refresh_failures_24h_uses_glob_not_like: requirement 2 defines refresh_failures_24h as a revoked_unix within the last 24h AND a revoked_reason beginning with the literal prefix refresh_. SQLite's LIKE operator treats a bare `_` as a single-character wildcard, so `LIKE 'refresh\_%'` would need an explicit ESCAPE clause to mean the literal underscore; Db::vault_stats instead uses `revoked_reason GLOB 'refresh_*'`, where GLOB's own wildcard alphabet (`*`/`?`/`[...]`) gives `_` no special meaning at all, so the literal-prefix match is exact with no escaping needed.
additional.provider_remove_not_found_code: AC6's own wording ("When the name is unknown, Then not_found") is a generic code this crate already has one precedent for (runs.rs's own literal "not_found" Structured code) rather than reusing connect_link's more specific vault_provider_not_found -- host.vault.provider_remove uses the same literal "not_found" code AC6 names.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent operator need a per-user, per-provider READ at all, rather than just retrying the call and reading whatever error comes back?
five_whys_trace.a: Problem statement: when a vault-injected call returns upstream_not_connected, the caller cannot tell whether the end user never connected, the token expired, or a refresh was rejected -- src/vault.rs's own pre-status resolve_for_call (P1 requirement 6, already shipped) reads and updates the vault_tokens row internally but reports nothing about it back to the caller beyond one generic refusal code, so recovering ("send a fresh connect link" vs "nothing to do, wait for the human") requires guessing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.vault.status need to keep naming a provider after host.vault.provider_remove deletes its registration (AC6), rather than simply dropping it from the listing the moment it's gone?
five_whys_trace.a: requirement 3 says provider_remove must mark every affected vault_tokens row provider_removed, and requirement 1 says status reports revoked_reason -- a caller who already has that user's status open, or who checks status right after being told about a rotation, needs to see WHY a previously-working connection is now dead, not just that the provider vanished from an unrelated listing (host.vault.providers) they'd have to separately think to check.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the operator need admin.vault.stats at all, rather than reading vault_tokens directly on the box?
five_whys_trace.a: Problem statement: the host operator could not count connected tokens or refresh failures on prod at all before this PRD -- none of the 44 pre-existing admin.* tools carried a vault entry, and the success-metrics table names 'vault state readable on prod' as the metric this PRD exists to move from 'no tool' to '200 with the operator tenant's provider'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does provider_set need OAuth presets (requirement 4) rather than always requiring the caller to paste auth_url/token_url by hand?
five_whys_trace.a: User stories: "an agent operator registers GitHub with preset: 'github' and only a client id and secret" -- every OAuth provider a tenant is likely to register (Slack, GitHub, Google) publishes fixed, well-known authorize/token endpoint URLs, so requiring them to be copied correctly on every provider_set call is pure copy-paste risk with no corresponding benefit; an explicit auth_url/token_url still overrides the preset per field, so a nonstandard or self-hosted OAuth app is never blocked by the preset table existing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC9 stay deferred rather than built as a branch-local test the same way AC1-8 were?
five_whys_trace.a: AC9's own Given is explicitly operator-provisioned ("done by hand from orch with the operator key on mcphost-1") and its When calls a real production endpoint (https://mcphost.dev/mcp) with the real operator/admin keys this coding sandbox does not have -- no branch-local TestServer can stand in for a real deploy, a real operator-registered placeholder-credential provider, or the admin key orch itself holds, so it is listed under deferred with reason operator-provisioned per the coder dispatch's own explicit instruction, not attempted with a mock that would prove nothing about the real prod surface.
